notebooks.title: Operational Criteria for Physical Causal Memory
notebooks.summary: Physical memory functions as an operational causal state when internal degrees of freedom enable predictive control over future system dynamics. This relationship is fundamentally limited by coarse-graining, which restricts access to exact Markovian trajectories and necessitates lower-bound inference on entropy production.
notebooks.findings:
Operational causal memory requires a persistent state to facilitate information transfer over time, which is strictly bounded by the accessibility of the underlying Markovian description. [source-6b1bb6af50ef4e9b] [peer-0916f25fdd8ff50318f79967]

Coarse-graining of physical dynamics imposes a fundamental limit on the objectivity of persistent memory, as it hides the microscopic process producing the observable state. [source-ee8169aea35a4ece] [peer-42ea5272a464585193f493cc]
notebooks.limitations: Existing models predominantly assume overdamped or Markovian dynamics. The mapping of these operational definitions to non-Markovian memory architectures remains under-constrained.
notebooks.next_questions: How does the precision of predictive control scale with the thermodynamic cost of maintaining specific internal pointer states in non-Markovian environments?
notebooks.reason: Revision to integrate coarse-graining limits on causal inference and predictive sufficiency.

notebooks.title: Thermodynamic Costs and Nonequilibrium Limits of Memory Retention
notebooks.summary: Revised analysis integrating open dissipative substrate models and nonequilibrium electrode conditions for reliable memory retention.
notebooks.findings: Memory writing and retention in open dissipative substrates entail thermodynamic entropy production bounds that extend Landauer's principle by incorporating synaptic degeneracy, coarse-graining, and nonequilibrium conditions. [source-bbac57fad2784d1b]
notebooks.limitations: Models remain specific to idealized bistable units and quantum dot assumptions; broad empirical validation across diverse biological and artificial media requires further work.
notebooks.next_questions: What are the precise scaling relations between memory refresh rates and entropy production in generic non-Markovian environments?

detail.title: Operational Criteria for Physical Causal Memory
detail.summary: Physical memory functions as an operational causal state when internal degrees of freedom enable predictive control over future system dynamics. This relationship is fundamentally limited by coarse-graining, which restricts access to exact Markovian trajectories and necessitates lower-bound inference on entropy production.
detail.findings:
Operational causal memory requires a persistent state to facilitate information transfer over time, which is strictly bounded by the accessibility of the underlying Markovian description. [source-6b1bb6af50ef4e9b] [peer-0916f25fdd8ff50318f79967]

Coarse-graining of physical dynamics imposes a fundamental limit on the objectivity of persistent memory, as it hides the microscopic process producing the observable state. [source-ee8169aea35a4ece] [peer-42ea5272a464585193f493cc]
detail.limitations: Existing models predominantly assume overdamped or Markovian dynamics. The mapping of these operational definitions to non-Markovian memory architectures remains under-constrained.
detail.next_questions: How does the precision of predictive control scale with the thermodynamic cost of maintaining specific internal pointer states in non-Markovian environments?
detail.reason: Revision to integrate coarse-graining limits on causal inference and predictive sufficiency.

review.alternative: Memory could arise from non-Markovian environmental correlations without requiring an explicit internal Markovian state.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence of persistent, stable memory formation in systems explicitly lacking local Markovian state structures.

detail.title: Dissipation Bounds in Predictive Information Engines
detail.summary: Revised analysis exploring how autonomous information engines use predictive internal states and how these states modulate thermodynamic dissipation.
detail.findings:
Energy conversion in autonomous information engines depends on information flow between working substances and internal states. [source-4c4f8663757e4564]

Dissipation bounds in stochastic systems can be examined through experiment and theory by exploring environmental coupling. [source-d8985518b1134b43]
detail.limitations: Models rely on specific stochastic thermodynamic frameworks; general lower bounds for noisy finite-memory systems remain constrained.
detail.next_questions: What are the exact scaling relations for noisy predictive feedback loops under varying thermal gradients?
detail.reason: Incorporating substantive source evidence into the notebook findings.

detail.title: Thermodynamic Costs and Nonequilibrium Limits of Memory Retention
detail.summary: Revised analysis integrating open dissipative substrate models and nonequilibrium electrode conditions for reliable memory retention.
detail.findings: Memory writing and retention in open dissipative substrates entail thermodynamic entropy production bounds that extend Landauer's principle by incorporating synaptic degeneracy, coarse-graining, and nonequilibrium conditions. [source-bbac57fad2784d1b]
detail.limitations: Models remain specific to idealized bistable units and quantum dot assumptions; broad empirical validation across diverse biological and artificial media requires further work.
detail.next_questions: What are the precise scaling relations between memory refresh rates and entropy production in generic non-Markovian environments?
